name: US Open Pool Championship 2023 – FINAL, Sky Sports overhead/end camera
source: training clip 1.mp4 (cut from YTSave ... IP-wATw-cus ... Gorst vs Ko Ping Chung ... 1080p.mp4)
frame: x along table: 0 = rail nearest camera (bottom of image) -> 100 far rail; y: 0 = left rail in image -> 50 right rail; z DOWN (bed z=0, ball centre z=-1.125). Same handedness as index.html (pocket 0=(0,0) bottom-left in image, 3=(0,50) bottom-right, 2=(100,0) far-left, 5=(100,50) far-right, 1/4 side pockets).
camera_summary: about 288in (7.3m) behind near rail, ~113in (2.9m) high, pitch 17.9 deg down, f=5727px (telephoto), principal point = image centre

T.world: x=100, z=0 (far cushion base on bed)

N.world: x=0, z=-1.43 (near cushion nose silhouette, subtle step 510->522 brightness)

validation.head_spot: cloth dot at px (960.3,738.8) projects to (25,25) – the dot pattern centre (960.8,727.6) is NOT the head spot (earlier wrong assumption, cost 2in at near end)
validation.ball_radius_px: observed vs predicted within 0.5px for coloured balls

ball_method: ball centre = camera ray through image circle centre intersected with plane z=-1.125. Circle: blob detection vs per-row bed colour, then radial edge search on upper ~200deg of outline + fixed-radius fit (radius from camera model). White cue ball needs this refinement (its shaded lower half matches the cloth).
reuse_rule: Same broadcast (US Open 2023, Sky overhead cam): run tools/pool_cv/edges.py+fitlines.py on one overhead frame per segment; if T/L/R lines move > ~2px, refit camera with linefit.py. Different event/venue (e.g. European Open 2023) = new calibration.
notes: Do NOT use the near-rail bright edge (y~879) as x=0: it is the outer edge of the near cushion top, not bed level.
